verdict.rationale: Isaac does not document a user-facing automation or scheduling feature. Its pipelines can still run unattended: Isaac Lab supports standalone headless operation from workstation to data center, Isaac Sim plugs into existing testing and validation pipelines, simulations can be driven programmatically via ROS 2 services, and custom synthetic-data pipelines can be built. That makes background automation achievable, but only through developer scripting and external orchestration. Missing for 10: a built-in way to define and schedule automations, triggers or recurring background jobs, monitoring of autonomous runs, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
